newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 5.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- State prosecutors will seek arrest warrants today for Sheen Kwang-shik and Woo Chan-mok, heads of two local banks on charges of bribery acceptance for providing preferential loans to the Hanbo Group.

- Kim Dae-jung, head of the National Congress for New Politics Party on Tueday urged President Kim Young-sam to quit his ruling New Korea Party and set up a supra-partisan cabinet to grapple with the current crises facing the nation.

- Governors in the western part of the United States have agreed to urge Washington to include South Korea in the Federal Visa Waiver Pilot Program, a Korea-US Economic Council spokesman said on Tuesday.
- The Taiwanese government has decided to provide economic aid totaling $1.5 billion to North Korea, a South Korean government source said on Tuesday.
